result.summary:
Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-024.md exactly as designed, no schema change (confirmed by the design's own header statement, DATA-DESIGNER not dispatched).

1. apps/bot/package.json: added `qrcode` (1.5.4, exact-pinned, no caret/tilde -- npm's current latest, verified via `npm view qrcode version`) to dependencies, per design §0.1's recommendation. Added devDependencies needed ONLY to satisfy AC3's literal wording ('decoded by an ACTUAL QR decoder', not just inspecting the encoder's input): `@types/qrcode` (1.5.6, qrcode itself ships no bundled types), `jsqr` (1.4.0, a real QR decoder), `pngjs` (7.0.0) + `@types/pngjs` (6.0.5, a real PNG decoder to turn the produced PNG bytes into raw pixels jsqr can read). All five pinned to an exact version, matching this project's dependency-pinning convention (decisions/0004/0005 precedent the design gate flagged).

2. apps/bot/src/domain/qr.ts (NEW): the single shared QR-image renderer, per design §2. `renderCheckInQrPng({botUsername, qrToken})` composes the exact template `https://t.me/<botUsername>?start=ci_<qrToken>` (no extra characters) and passes it to `QRCode.toBuffer(text, {type:'png'})`, returning a fresh Buffer on every call. Framework-free (decisions/0004): no grammy import, no DbClient dependency, no I/O beyond the one qrcode library call.

3. apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts: NEW `getMyRegistrations(db, userId)` per design §1/§0.3 -- one SELECT joining registrations -> events -> chapters (the same two-join shape getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone already uses), `WHERE registrations.user_id = userId` as the ONLY filter (every admission state returned, no admission-IN filter, per the design's explicit AC4 reasoning), ordered by `registrations.created_at DESC`. The function's signature has exactly one parameter (`userId`) -- no eventId/registrationId or any other caller-suppliable identifier anywhere in it, making the privacy scoping structural per §0.3 point 2. getWaitlistPosition/decideWithdrawOutcome/formatDateTimeInTimezone are all reused UNCHANGED, called per-row by the handler (not by this function itself, which performs no per-row I/O beyond its one SELECT), exactly as §1 specifies.

4. apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts: `STATUS_CATALOG_KEY` given an `export` keyword (the only change to this file, per design §4's closing note) so handlers/my.ts can reuse the existing status-key mapping directly rather than a second copy being written.

5. apps/bot/src/handlers/my.ts (NEW): `makeMyCommandHandler(db)` per design §3. Step 1 defensive tgId guard; step 2 `resolveActingUser(db, BigInt(tgId))` -- the ONLY place a user identity enters this path, sourced from Telegram's own authenticated sender id (§0.3 step 1), replying `profile.startFirst` and returning if null; step 3 `getMyRegistrations(db, actingUser.id)` (§0.3 step 2); step 4 empty list -> `catalog.my.emptyState`, return; step 5 non-empty -> one `catalog.my.header` preamble reply, then one message per row in the order returned: (a) two `formatDateTimeInTimezone` calls for start/end; (c) `getWaitlistPosition` called ONLY for waitlisted rows, live and never cached (REQ-021's own contract, satisfying AC2); (d) composed text = [status line via the reused STATUS_CATALOG_KEY, event title, date/time, optional waitlist-position line]; (e) the withdraw button attached via the exact literal `withdraw:confirm:<registrationId>` callback_data REQ-022's existing WITHDRAW_CONFIRM_PATTERN/handler already matches (design §0.2 -- withdraw.ts is UNTOUCHED), shown iff `decideWithdrawOutcome({registrationExists:true, ownerUserId:actingUser.id, actingUserId:actingUser.id, admission:row.admission, checkedInAt:row.checkedInAt}).kind === 'withdrawn'` (ownerUserId===actingUserId always by construction here, so 'not-owner' can never fire from this call site, per §0.2's own stated reasoning); (f) the QR gate (AC3/AC4): iff `admission==='admitted' && qrToken!==null`, calls `renderCheckInQrPng({botUsername: ctx.me.username, qrToken})` and sends via `ctx.replyWithPhoto(new InputFile(png), {caption: text, reply_markup?})` instead of plain `ctx.reply` -- every other admission state falls through to plain text. One message per row (never one giant concatenated message), matching the design's own stated structural reasoning (a QR image can only ride a photo message, and each row's withdraw button needs its own reply_markup).

6. apps/bot/src/index.ts: registered `bot.command('my', makeMyCommandHandler(db))`, alongside the other id-less, non-organizer-gated read commands (/events, /withdraw), per design §3's own placement note.

7. i18n: new `Catalog.my` section (header/emptyState/withdrawButton) added to apps/bot/src/i18n/{types,ru,en}.ts per design §4 -- placeholder/minimal functional copy per decisions/0002, CONTENT-BA owns final wording. Row text composition reuses `catalog.registration.*` status keys directly, exactly as §4 specifies (no second, parallel status-string set introduced).

Test additions:
- apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts (NEW, no DB needed): renderCheckInQrPng, real-decode proof for AC3 -- decodes the actual produced PNG bytes with jsqr (a real QR decoder) fed pngjs-decoded raw pixels (a real PNG decoder), asserting the decoded string is EXACTLY `https://t.me/<botUsername>?start=ci_<qrToken>` and contains the AC's named substring `?start=ci_<qrToken>` -- this does NOT just inspect the string passed to the encoder. Second case confirms a fresh Buffer object is produced on every call (no caching) while its bytes are byte-identical for identical input.
- apps/bot/src/handlers/my.test.ts (NEW, real scratch Postgres via bot.handleUpdate()): AC1 -- two users (Alice/Bob) registered for the SAME event, each with a distinct seeded Profile (firstName/lastName/company/phone/email); dispatching /my as each and scanning EVERY captured payload (JSON-serialized, with the InputFile-bearing 'photo' key stripped since InputFile's own toJSON() deliberately throws) confirms neither response contains the other's name/company/phone/email/tgId/registrationId anywhere -- each response contains only its own registrationId. AC2 -- capacity-0 event (both registrations land waitlisted), viewer's row genuinely behind another row; captures position=2, withdraws the ahead row via the REAL withdraw flow (handlers/withdraw.ts's own confirm callback, unchanged), re-invokes /my: position=1, and the viewer's own row's `updated_at` is read back byte-identical (`toEqual`) to before -- confirming getMyRegistrations performs zero writes of its own. AC3/AC4/AC5 -- one user with four registrations across four events (admitted+qrToken, withdrawn, rejected, waitlisted); asserts exactly 1 sendPhoto (the admitted row) and exactly 3 sendMessage (the other three, none carrying a 'photo' field); the one photo's raw Buffer (InputFile.fileData) is decoded with the same jsqr+pngjs pipeline and matches `https://t.me/test_bot?start=ci_<qrToken>` exactly -- proving AC3 against the real send path (not qr.test.ts's unit-level renderer call) and AC4's negative cases in the same run. AC5 is verified structurally: handlers/my.ts imports and calls domain/qr.ts's renderCheckInQrPng (grep-verifiable), never re-implementing QR encoding inline.

All DB-backed tests ran against a real, migrated scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432) -- started fresh for this run (container did not already exist) and migrated via `drizzle-kit migrate`; left running afterward for REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER's convenience.

One environment note unrelated to this requirement's own code, disclosed for transparency: this machine's npm (11.5.1) regenerates package-lock.json with a pruned optional-dependency set (fewer per-platform native-binding entries than the previously committed lockfile) the first time `npm install` runs at all on it, independent of which packages are being added -- confirmed by reproducing the same large diff via a plain `npm install --workspace=apps/bot` against the ORIGINAL committed lockfile with no new deps yet added. The five new bot dependencies (qrcode/jsqr/pngjs/@types/qrcode/@types/pngjs) are correctly present in the resulting lockfile; the rest of the diff is this pre-existing npm-version/lockfile-format mismatch, not a deliberate change. A native binding vitest's own Vite config needs (`@rolldown/binding-win32-x64-msvc`) had to be installed with `--no-save --no-package-lock` to actually run the suite on this machine -- this is the exact workaround vitest's own startup error message names for a known npm optional-dependency bug (npm/cli#4828); it does not appear in the committed lockfile diff.

Commands run from the REPO ROOT: `npm run lint --workspace=apps/bot` -> exit 0, 0 errors. `npm run build --workspace=apps/bot` -> exit 0, tsc clean. `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, no path filter) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. 217 = REQ-023's own confirmed baseline of 211 + 6 new cases (2 in qr.test.ts + 3 in my.test.ts's three describe blocks... actually 2+3=5 new test cases, plus REQ-023's suite already included the withdraw flow my.test.ts also exercises -- see evidence.commands for the exact verbose re-run confirming all 5 AC-covering cases individually). `git status --porcelain` confirms only the files listed in artifacts_out plus package.json/package-lock.json are dirty, all under apps/bot/** or the root lockfile a new bot dependency requires; no file touched outside the requirement's declared surface.

commands: npm view qrcode version -> 1.5.4; npm view @types/qrcode version -> 1.5.6; npm view jsqr version -> 1.4.0; npm view pngjs version -> 7.0.0; npm view @types/pngjs version -> 6.0.5
npm install (repo root, after editing apps/bot/package.json) -> new deps recorded in package-lock.json (verified via grep for "qrcode"/"jsqr"/"pngjs" in package-lock.json)
cd apps/bot && docker compose up -d -> bot-postgres-1 started fresh (network+volume created)
DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npm run migrate -> migrations applied successfully
npm run build --workspace=apps/bot -> exit 0, tsc clean
npm install @rolldown/binding-win32-x64-msvc --no-save --no-package-lock -> resolves a pre-existing local Vite/vitest native-binding gap (npm/cli#4828), no committed-file effect
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root, full suite) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

same command scoped to apps/bot/src/handlers/my.test.ts apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts --reporter=verbose -> 5/5 passed individually: AC1, AC2, AC3/AC4/AC5 (my.test.ts) + the real-decode proof + the fresh-buffer case (qr.test.ts)

git status --porcelain -> only apps/bot/package.json, apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/registration.ts, apps/bot/src/i18n/{en,ru,types}.ts, apps/bot/src/index.ts, package-lock.json modified; apps/bot/src/domain/qr.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/qr.test.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/my.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/my.test.ts new -- nothing outside this set

ac_results.AC1: PASS -- handlers/my.test.ts: Alice and Bob, distinct seeded Profiles (name/company/phone/email), both registered admitted for the SAME event; each user's captured /my reply set (photo caption + text + reply_markup, JSON-serialized) contains ZERO occurrence of the other's firstName/lastName/company/phone/email/tgId/registrationId; each contains only its own registrationId in its own withdraw button's callback_data
ac_results.AC2: PASS -- handlers/my.test.ts: capacity-0 event, two waitlisted rows (ahead, viewer); /my shows the viewer at position 2; the ahead registration is withdrawn via the real /withdraw confirm-callback flow; /my re-invoked shows position 1; the viewer's own registrations row's updated_at is read back byte-identical (toEqual) across both invocations -- getMyRegistrations/getWaitlistPosition perform zero writes
ac_results.AC3: PASS (real decoder, both at the unit level and through the actual send path) -- qr.test.ts: renderCheckInQrPng's produced PNG, decoded with jsqr fed pngjs-decoded pixels, yields exactly `https://t.me/<botUsername>?start=ci_<qrToken>`, containing the AC-named `?start=ci_<qrToken>` substring. my.test.ts: the one sendPhoto call's real InputFile buffer, decoded the same way, yields exactly `https://t.me/test_bot?start=ci_<the admitted row's own qrToken>`
ac_results.AC4: PASS -- my.test.ts: of four rows (admitted, withdrawn, rejected, waitlisted) for the same user, exactly 1 sendPhoto (the admitted one) and exactly 3 sendMessage occur; none of the three plain-text sends carries a 'photo' field
ac_results.AC5: PASS -- structural: handlers/my.ts's only QR-related import is `renderCheckInQrPng` from domain/qr.ts, called once in step 5f; no QR-encoding logic is duplicated inline in the handler (grep-verifiable: `QRCode`/`qrcode` package import appears nowhere in handlers/my.ts)

issues.title: package-lock.json diff includes pre-existing npm-version optional-dependency pruning, unrelated to this requirement's own dependency additions
issues.description: This machine's npm 11.5.1 regenerates package-lock.json with fewer per-platform native-binding optionalDependency entries (e.g. most non-Windows @rolldown/binding-* variants) than the currently committed lockfile, the FIRST time npm install runs at all -- reproduced independently against the original committed lockfile with zero new packages added, so it is not something this requirement's five new bot dependencies caused. The five new dependencies (qrcode, jsqr, pngjs, @types/qrcode, @types/pngjs) are correctly present in the resulting lockfile. Flagged as INFO rather than routed back since it does not touch capacity/consent/data-visibility rules and does not change what actually installs on this platform; a future CI run on a different OS/arch may want to re-verify its own optional-dependency resolution is unaffected.
